questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Solving for cruising duration from total distance under a trapezoidal velocity-time graph

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Solving for cruising duration from total distance under a trapezoidal velocity-time graph

hints: The total time for the journey is $10 + T + 15 = T + 25\text{ s}$.
Set the area of the trapezium equal to $950$: $\frac{T + (T + 25)}{2} \times 20 = 10(2T + 25) = 950 \implies 2T + 25 = 95 \implies T = 35\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the total distance as the area of a trapezium with parallel bases $T$ and $T + 25$, and height $20$:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{T + (T + 25)}{2} \times 20 = 10(2T + 25) = 20T + 250$$

Equate the area to the given distance of $950\text{ m}$ and solve for $T$:
$$20T + 250 = 950 \implies 20T = 700$$
$$T = \frac{700}{20} = 35\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up trapezium area equation:
- Parallel bases are $T$ and $T + 25$:
$$10(2T + 25) = 950$$

Solve for cruising duration $T$:
- Simplifying:
$$2T + 25 = 95 \implies 2T = 70 \implies T = 35\text{ s}$$
The car cruises for $35\text{ s}$.

$$16 - 6a = 6a \implies 12a = 16 \implies a = \frac{16}{12} = \frac{4}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Relate intermediate velocity across stages:
- End of first stage:
$$v_1 = 16 - 6a$$
- Start of stopping stage:
$$v_1 = 3a \times 2 = 6a$$

Solve for acceleration parameter $a$:
- Equating:
$$16 - 6a = 6a \implies 12a = 16 \implies a = \frac{4}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The base deceleration is $\frac{4}{3}\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:

- Trapezium with bases $25\text{ s}$ and $50\text{ s}$:
$$\frac{25 + 50}{2} \times V = 37.5V$$

Solve for top speed $V$:
- Dividing distance by half-base sum:
$$V = \frac{720}{37.5} = 19.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Acceleration time is $t_{\text{acc}} = \frac{V}{1.0} = V$, distance is $s_{\text{acc}} = \frac{V^2}{2(1.0)} = 0.5V^2$.
Deceleration time is $t_{\text{dec}} = \frac{V}{2.0} = 0.5V$, distance is $s_{\text{dec}} = \frac{V^2}{2(2.0)} = 0.25V^2$.
The combined distance for acceleration and deceleration is $0.5V^2 + 0.25V^2 = 0.75V^2$.
The cruising distance is $2400 - 0.75V^2$, so cruising time is $t_{\text{cruise}} = \frac{2400 - 0.75V^2}{V} = \frac{2400}{V} - 0.75V$.

Sum durations: $T = V + 0.5V + \frac{2400}{V} - 0.75V = 0.75V + \frac{2400}{V}$. For a cruising phase to exist, $0.75V^2 \le 2400 \implies V \le \sqrt{3200} = 40\sqrt{2} \approx 56.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Derive the times and distances for the acceleration and deceleration stages in terms of $V$:
$$t_{\text{acc}} = \frac{V}{a} = \frac{V}{1.0} = V, \quad s_{\text{acc}} = \frac{V^2}{2a} = 0.5V^2$$
$$t_{\text{dec}} = \frac{V}{d} = \frac{V}{2.0} = 0.5V, \quad s_{\text{dec}} = \frac{V^2}{2d} = 0.25V^2$$

Express the cruising duration and total journey time $T$:
$$s_{\text{cruise}} = 2400 - (s_{\text{acc}} + s_{\text{dec}}) = 2400 - 0.75V^2$$
$$t_{\text{cruise}} = \frac{s_{\text{cruise}}}{V} = \frac{2400}{V} - 0.75V$$
$$T = t_{\text{acc}} + t_{\text{dec}} + t_{\text{cruise}} = 1.5V + \left(\frac{2400}{V} - 0.75V\right) = 0.75V + \frac{2400}{V}$$

Find the maximum possible speed for which cruising distance is non-negative:
$$s_{\text{cruise}} \ge 0 \implies 0.75V^2 \le 2400 \implies V^2 \le 3200$$
$$V_{\max} = \sqrt{3200} = 40\sqrt{2} \approx 56.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Derive speed-dependent stage durations and distances:
- Acceleration and deceleration totals:
$$t_{\text{acc}} + t_{\text{dec}} = V + 0.5V = 1.5V$$
$$s_{\text{acc}} + s_{\text{dec}} = 0.5V^2 + 0.25V^2 = 0.75V^2$$

Combine with cruising segment:
- Cruising duration:
$$t_{\text{cruise}} = \frac{2400 - 0.75V^2}{V} = \frac{2400}{V} - 0.75V$$
- Total time:
$$T = 1.5V - 0.75V + \frac{2400}{V} = 0.75V + \frac{2400}{V}$$

Evaluate boundary condition:
- Non-negative cruising condition:
$$0.75V^2 \le 2400 \implies V_{\max} = \sqrt{3200} = 40\sqrt{2} \approx 56.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The formula is established and $V_{\max} \approx 56.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
